title: Invalid Data Received From Door Switch Module - Passenger
shortDescription: Implausible data from the passenger door switch module.
fullDescription:
U0836 reports invalid passenger-door module data on the CAN/LIN network. Like its driver-side counterpart, the fault usually comes from flex damage in the door jamb, water ingress, or an internal module fault.

The passenger door module typically handles window, lock, and mirror commands on that side; loss of valid data disables those conveniences but rarely affects drivability.
safetyImpact: Passenger window and lock convenience features may be lost; no drivability impact.

causes.cause: Water intrusion into passenger door module

symptoms: Passenger window inoperative from driver switch

fixSteps.title: Live data flex test
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle door harness while viewing passenger door module status.

fixSteps.title: Inspect module and harness
fixSteps.instruction: Pull door panel, check for water damage and corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Repair harness or swap the passenger door module as required.

faq.q: Does this fail state disable airbags?
faq.a: No — side airbags are on a separate safety network.

title: Invalid Data Received From Door Switch Module - Rear Left
shortDescription: Implausible rear-left door switch module data.
fullDescription:
U0841 sets when the BCM sees malformed or out-of-range data from the left-rear door module. The fault is almost always localized to that door — jamb harness, water intrusion, or the module itself — and does not affect vehicle drivability.

On vehicles without a dedicated rear-door module, this code can be set by a faulty door ajar switch reporting impossible state transitions to the BCM.
safetyImpact: Rear door ajar warning and child-lock indication may be incorrect.

causes.cause: Jamb harness break on rear-left door

fixSteps.title: Actuate door
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle the rear-left door open and closed while watching live data.

fixSteps.title: Replace ajar switch
fixSteps.instruction: If signal is implausible, replace the rear-left door ajar / latch-integrated switch.

faq.q: Will this drain the battery?
faq.a: Yes — a stuck door-ajar signal keeps interior lights on and can kill the battery overnight.

title: Invalid Data Received From Door Switch Module - Rear Right
shortDescription: Implausible rear-right door switch module data.
fullDescription:
U0848 is the right-rear counterpart of U0841. The BCM is seeing implausible data from the right-rear door switch/module, usually from a failed ajar switch or jamb harness break.

Diagnosis and repair mirror the left-rear side.
safetyImpact: Rear door ajar indication may be incorrect; minimal drivability impact.

fixSteps.title: Test door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Watch door status live as you cycle the door — note any missed transitions.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch or harness
fixSteps.instruction: Replace faulty latch/ajar switch or repair jamb wiring.

faq.q: Can I just unplug the switch to clear it?
faq.a: Unplugging sets a different code (missing module) — replace the switch instead.

title: Invalid Data Received From Tire Pressure Monitor Module
shortDescription: TPMS module is sending data that other modules cannot validate.
fullDescription:
U0872 indicates the receiving module (typically the BCM or instrument cluster) is getting malformed data from the TPMS control module. Common causes include a corrupted TPMS module configuration, damaged antenna, or failing sensors that confuse the controller.

The result is usually a TPMS warning light that cannot be cleared and pressure displays showing dashes or obviously wrong values.
safetyImpact: Driver loses reliable tire pressure monitoring, increasing risk of blowouts from underinflation.

causes.cause: Failed or low-battery TPMS sensors confusing the module
Module not relearned after tire rotation

fixSteps.title: Scan TPMS module directly
fixSteps.instruction: Connect a TPMS-capable scanner and read sensor IDs and battery status for each wheel.

fixSteps.title: Replace weak sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Replace any sensor below threshold battery or not responding.

fixSteps.title: Relearn positions
fixSteps.instruction: Perform the factory relearn procedure to pair sensors to their corners.

fixSteps.title: Replace TPMS module
fixSteps.instruction: If invalid data persists with good sensors, replace the TPMS control module.

faq.q: Can cold weather cause this?
faq.a: Cold weather drops sensor battery voltage and can trigger transient U0872 — warm and retest before replacement.

title: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module B
shortDescription: Secondary body control module is transmitting implausible data.
fullDescription:
Some vehicles run multiple body-control modules (BCM-A for front cabin, BCM-B for rear/cargo). U0886 indicates invalid data from BCM-B. Symptoms typically revolve around rear cabin features — power liftgate, rear HVAC controls, third-row power features.

Root causes match a primary BCM fault: bad ground, corrupted flash, CAN bus issues, or internal hardware failure.
safetyImpact: Rear lighting, liftgate, or convenience features may fail or behave erratically.

causes.cause: CAN wiring fault near rear of vehicle

fixSteps.title: Check voltages
fixSteps.instruction: Verify battery voltage and BCM-B power/ground.

fixSteps.title: Inspect CAN to BCM-B
fixSteps.instruction: Check CAN pair continuity and termination at BCM-B connector.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram or replace BCM-B
fixSteps.instruction: Attempt reflash first; replace if hardware is confirmed bad.

faq.q: Is BCM-B user-serviceable?
faq.a: Replacement is DIY-doable but programming typically requires dealer-level tools.

title: Invalid Data Received From Driver's Seat Control Module
shortDescription: Driver seat module is sending implausible data on the bus.
fullDescription:
U0890 is set when the BCM or HVAC/climate module receives malformed data from the driver seat control module — heated/ventilated seat state, memory position, occupant classification flags. Causes are typically water intrusion under the seat, a crushed harness, or a damaged module from spilled drinks.

Because the driver seat module often feeds occupant classification to the SRS/airbag system on some platforms, clearing this code is important for airbag readiness.
safetyImpact: May impair memory seat, heating, ventilation, and on some vehicles airbag deployment logic.

fixSteps.title: Inspect under seat
fixSteps.instruction: Slide seat fully forward and back; check harness and module for damage or moisture.

fixSteps.title: Check connector
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and inspect the main seat connector for bent/corroded pins.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in known-good seat module; may require programming.

faq.q: Why did a coffee spill kill my seat module?
faq.a: Sugar in drinks corrodes the circuit board; even a small spill can bridge traces and cause chronic faults.

title: Invalid Data Received From Body Control Module A Mirror
shortDescription: Mirror control data from the BCM is implausible.
fullDescription:
U0900 reports that the mirror portion of the BCM-A broadcast is invalid. Exterior mirror folding, heating, and memory features rely on this data; a fault disables those conveniences. Auto-dim and tilt-in-reverse functions may also be affected.

Issues typically trace to a short inside the mirror assembly, a damaged door harness, or a corroded pin in the mirror connector.
safetyImpact: Loss of power mirror adjust, heat, or tilt-in-reverse can reduce visibility.

fixSteps.title: Command mirrors with scan tool
fixSteps.instruction: Actuate mirror functions with bidirectional control to confirm fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect mirror wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check door jamb harness and mirror connector for damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace mirror or switch
fixSteps.instruction: Swap mirror assembly or switch as indicated.

faq.q: Why do both mirrors quit together?
faq.a: Both mirrors share a common driver circuit inside the BCM — one BCM failure stops both.

title: Invalid Data Received From Front Control Module
shortDescription: Front control module (FCM) data is implausible on the bus.
fullDescription:
U0920 is set when another controller receives implausible data from the Front Control Module — a module common on Chrysler/RAM platforms that drives headlights, horns, wipers, and cooling fan relays. Faults typically manifest as multi-circuit issues: e.g., wipers plus headlights plus horn simultaneously misbehaving.

Because the FCM lives in the front of the vehicle, it is exposed to water and road salt — corrosion is a frequent root cause.
safetyImpact: May lose headlights, wipers, or horn — all safety-critical functions.

causes.cause: CAN bus wiring damage near FCM

fixSteps.title: Locate and inspect FCM
fixSteps.instruction: Find the FCM (usually in the fuse/junction box area) and check for corrosion and water damage.

fixSteps.title: Test FCM outputs
fixSteps.instruction: Command outputs with a bidirectional scanner to see which circuits fail.

fixSteps.title: Replace FCM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and program the FCM to the VIN.

faq.q: Can I seal the FCM instead of replacing it?
faq.a: Only as a temporary fix — once water has reached the circuit board, corrosion will continue.

title: Invalid Data Received From Remote Function Actuation
shortDescription: RFA (keyless entry) module data is invalid.
fullDescription:
U0950 sets when the BCM receives implausible data from the Remote Function Actuation module — the controller that decodes key-fob commands and passive-entry requests. The result is usually intermittent or total loss of remote unlock, remote start, and passive entry.

Causes include water damage to the RFA antenna/module (often under the driver seat or in the C-pillar), a failing antenna, or internal module fault.
safetyImpact: Convenience only — keyless entry may not work, but physical key still operates the vehicle.

fixSteps.title: Replace fob batteries
fixSteps.instruction: Rule out weak batteries first — cheapest possible fix.

fixSteps.title: Locate RFA module
fixSteps.instruction: Check under driver seat or in C-pillar for water damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace RFA module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and program to the VIN; reprogram keyfobs.

faq.q: Why do my fobs work some days and not others?
faq.a: Water-damaged modules are temperature sensitive — they may work cold and fail when hot.

title: Honda - ECM/PCM Data Link Failure
shortDescription: Honda-specific loss of communication between ECM/PCM and other modules.
fullDescription:
U1130 on Honda vehicles indicates the engine control module has lost serial communication with the rest of the network. Honda uses a proprietary K-line and F-CAN blend; U1130 typically points to a broken or shorted F-CAN pair or a faulty ECM ground.

Affected systems include the gauge cluster, VSA/ABS, and automatic transmission, all of which rely on engine RPM and torque data from the ECM.
safetyImpact: Loss of gauge cluster data, potential stall, ABS and stability control disabled.

fixSteps.title: Check DLC CAN pins
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance between DLC pins 6 and 14 — should be ~60 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ECM connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check ECM main connector for bent pins and water.

fixSteps.title: Verify ECM ground
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm ECM ground on transmission/engine has less than 0.1 ohm to battery negative.

fixSteps.title: Replace/reprogram ECM
fixSteps.instruction: If diagnostics confirm, replace ECM and flash with Honda HDS.

faq.q: Is this the same as a dealer-only repair?
faq.a: ECM flashing requires HDS, but wiring and ground repair can be done independently.

title: Honda - Ignition Signal Communication Error
shortDescription: Honda network fault related to ignition/crank signal broadcast.
fullDescription:
U1135 on Honda indicates the ignition/run signal broadcast from the BCM or ignition switch module to the ECM/PCM is missing or implausible. The code usually appears alongside no-start, stall, or intermittent running conditions.

Typical causes include a worn ignition switch, corroded under-dash harness, or a failed immobilizer/BCM.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may not start or stall in traffic.

fixSteps.title: Cycle key and watch data
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle the key while watching ignition-run status on a scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace ignition switch
fixSteps.instruction: If signal drops during cycle, replace the electrical portion of the ignition switch.

fixSteps.title: BCM reprogramming
fixSteps.instruction: If switch is good, reflash or replace BCM.

faq.q: Will a jiggle of the key fix it temporarily?
faq.a: Yes — but that's a clear sign the switch is failing and should be replaced.

title: Honda - SRS/Airbag Module Communication Error
shortDescription: Honda SRS module not communicating correctly on the bus.
fullDescription:
U1148 indicates the Honda SRS/airbag module is not communicating or is sending invalid data. Because SRS is safety-critical, U1148 usually triggers an airbag warning lamp and disables deployment in some fault modes.

Root causes are typically under-seat SRS connectors disturbed during service, corrosion, or internal SRS module fault.
safetyImpact: Airbags may not deploy in a crash.

fixSteps.title: Reseat under-seat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, wait 5 minutes, then reseat yellow SRS connectors under both front seats.

fixSteps.title: Clear and test
fixSteps.instruction: Clear codes with HDS and road-test.

fixSteps.title: Replace SRS module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if a hard fault is found; requires coding to VIN.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive?
faq.a: Only short distances — with SRS disabled, airbags may not deploy.

title: Honda - Gauge Cluster Communication Error
shortDescription: Honda instrument cluster not communicating.
fullDescription:
U1160 indicates the Honda instrument cluster (gauge assembly) has lost or corrupted communication with the rest of the network. Typical symptoms include blank gauges, stuck mileage, or warning lights flashing erratically.

Causes range from a corroded dash connector to an internal cluster fault (a well-known issue on older Accord/Civic models where cold-solder joints fail with heat cycling).
safetyImpact: Driver loses speed, RPM, and warning indications.

fixSteps.title: Check cluster power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify battery and ignition power at the cluster connector.

fixSteps.title: Reflow or replace cluster
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the cluster or have the circuit board reflowed by a specialty shop.

faq.q: Can I swap a junkyard cluster?
faq.a: Yes, but mileage will not transfer without a cluster programmer.

title: Mazda - Configuration Mismatch
shortDescription: Mazda module configuration data does not match the vehicle.
fullDescription:
U1150 on Mazda indicates a module (often the BCM or TCM) holds configuration/coding data that does not match the VIN or option content. It typically shows up after module replacement or after a software update was interrupted.

The fix is re-running the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System configuration procedure — no wiring or hardware fault required.
safetyImpact: Affected module's features may be disabled until configuration completes.

fixSteps.title: Connect IDS
fixSteps.instruction: Connect Mazda MDARS/IDS and query the offending module's configuration.

fixSteps.title: Run as-built reprogram
fixSteps.instruction: Apply the factory as-built file to the module.

faq.q: Is there a generic alternative to IDS?
faq.a: Only a few high-end aftermarket tools can perform Mazda as-built programming.

title: Mazda - Security Access Denied
shortDescription: Mazda scan tool security handshake failed.
fullDescription:
U1156 sets when a scan tool or replacement module fails the Mazda security access challenge. Usually this happens when an aftermarket tool lacks Mazda security licensing, or when an attempted programming session was interrupted.

The code does not indicate a hardware fault — resolve by using proper Mazda IDS/MDARS with valid security credentials.
safetyImpact: No drivability impact; indicates programming/security issue only.

fixSteps.title: Use licensed tool
fixSteps.instruction: Retry with Mazda MDARS or a tool with proper security credentials.

fixSteps.title: Recover module
fixSteps.instruction: If module is bricked, use IDS recovery routine.

faq.q: Can I clear this with a generic OBD-II reader?
faq.a: No — you must complete a successful security-authenticated session to clear it.

title: Mazda - TCM Communication Malfunction
shortDescription: Mazda transmission control module communication fault.
fullDescription:
U1180 on Mazda indicates the TCM has lost or is sending invalid data on the powertrain CAN. Typical symptoms are harsh shifts, failure to shift out of limp mode, and a warning lamp in the cluster.

Causes typically include the common Mazda TCM connector corrosion (well documented on CX-5/CX-9), CAN wiring damage, or internal TCM fault.
safetyImpact: Transmission may remain in limp mode, limiting speed and acceleration.

fixSteps.title: Inspect TCM connector
fixSteps.instruction: Remove TCM connector and check for the known corrosion issue on Mazda platforms.

fixSteps.title: Clean and seal
fixSteps.instruction: Clean connector and apply dielectric grease; reseat and retest.

fixSteps.title: Replace TCM
fixSteps.instruction: If internal fault is confirmed, replace and program with IDS.

faq.q: Is the connector corrosion covered under warranty?
faq.a: Mazda issued TSBs for specific model/year combinations — check with your dealer.

title: Mazda - High-Speed CAN Communication Fault
shortDescription: Mazda high-speed CAN bus general fault.
fullDescription:
U1259 on Mazda is a general high-speed CAN bus malfunction code. It accompanies widespread U-codes and indicates the bus is shorted, open, or missing termination.

Start diagnosis at the DLC: 60 ohms between CAN-H and CAN-L means bus and termination are good; other readings identify the fault type.
safetyImpact: Widespread loss of vehicle communication, multiple systems disabled.

causes.cause: CAN bus short to ground or power
Failed termination resistor in a module

fixSteps.title: Measure DLC resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Key off, measure between pins 6 and 14 — should be 60 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect modules
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug modules one at a time while watching bus voltage to isolate the faulty one.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring or module
fixSteps.instruction: Repair damaged CAN wiring or replace the offending module.

faq.q: Can one bad module kill the whole bus?
faq.a: Yes — a module with an internal short pulls the CAN pair to ground and silences every controller.

title: Hyundai - Vehicle Identification Mismatch
shortDescription: Hyundai module reports a VIN mismatch.
fullDescription:
U1234 on Hyundai indicates two modules disagree about the VIN programmed into them. This commonly occurs after a used module is installed or after a software flash went wrong.

The fix is to rewrite the VIN in the mismatched module using GDS/KDS. No hardware repair is needed.
safetyImpact: Some features (immobilizer, audio entitlements) may be disabled until resolved.

fixSteps.title: Connect GDS/KDS
fixSteps.instruction: Connect Hyundai scan tool and read VIN from each module.

fixSteps.title: Write VIN
fixSteps.instruction: Use VIN-write function to align all modules.

faq.q: Can I buy a used module and program it?
faq.a: Only if the donor module supports VIN rewrite — otherwise you must buy new.

title: Hyundai - CAN Bus Circuit Low
shortDescription: Hyundai CAN bus voltage is below the valid range.
fullDescription:
U1300 on Hyundai indicates the CAN bus is reading abnormally low voltage — often from a short to ground on the CAN-H line or a failed module pulling the bus down. This leaves many modules unable to communicate.

Diagnose by measuring CAN-H and CAN-L at the DLC while systematically disconnecting modules.
safetyImpact: Widespread module communication loss; may cause no-start.

fixSteps.title: Check DLC voltages
fixSteps.instruction: Key on, measure CAN-H (~3.5V) and CAN-L (~1.5V) at the DLC.

fixSteps.title: Isolate faulty module
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect modules one at a time; bus voltage normalizes when faulty module is unplugged.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Repair harness short or replace faulty module.

faq.q: Why does my scanner lose connection sometimes?
faq.a: Intermittent short drops bus voltage enough that the scan tool handshake fails.

title: Hyundai - CAN Bus Circuit High
shortDescription: Hyundai CAN bus voltage is above the valid range.
fullDescription:
U1400 indicates the CAN bus is reading high — typically CAN-H shorted to 12V or a module with an internal pull-up defect. All modules downstream of the fault lose communication.

Start at the DLC, check voltages, and isolate the offending module by selective disconnection.
safetyImpact: Widespread communication loss, potential no-start.

fixSteps.title: Measure CAN voltages
fixSteps.instruction: Look for CAN-H above 4V with key on — indicates short to power.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness near power
fixSteps.instruction: Check routing near fuse/junction boxes for chafed insulation.

fixSteps.title: Repair harness
fixSteps.instruction: Repair short and verify with DLC voltage readings.

faq.q: Can a blown fuse cause this?
faq.a: No — a fuse blowing usually kills a module, not the bus.

title: Kia - Serial Communication Link Failure
shortDescription: Kia serial/CAN link error between modules.
fullDescription:
U1600 on Kia indicates a serial communication link failure between two modules — typically BCM and cluster or BCM and smart-key unit. Kia platforms are known for moisture-related BCM failures that trigger this code.

Inspect the BCM first, then the LIN/CAN harness, before replacing modules.
safetyImpact: Warning lamps, door-ajar, and keyless entry may malfunction.

fixSteps.title: Scan modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use KDS to scan BCM and related modules.

fixSteps.title: Inspect BCM area
fixSteps.instruction: Check under-dash for water stains near BCM.

fixSteps.title: Replace BCM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace BCM and program to VIN.

faq.q: Is this covered under extended warranty?
faq.a: Some Kia platforms had BCM water-intrusion campaigns — check with your dealer by VIN.

title: Kia - Smart Key Module Communication Error
shortDescription: Kia smart-key unit not communicating correctly.
fullDescription:
U1700 on Kia indicates loss of communication with the Smart Key Unit (SMK). Symptoms include failure of push-button start, passive entry, and immobilizer rejection.

Common causes are antenna faults, water damage, or SMK internal failure.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may fail to start, stranding driver.

fixSteps.title: Try backup start
fixSteps.instruction: Use the emergency fob-on-button method to confirm fob is working.

fixSteps.title: Inspect SMK location
fixSteps.instruction: Check SMK in dash for water damage and connector seating.

fixSteps.title: Replace SMK
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and program via Kia KDS.

faq.q: Why does the car start sometimes but not others?
faq.a: Water-damaged SMKs are temperature-sensitive — they work cold and fail when heat-soaked.

title: Subaru - ECM CAN Communication Error
shortDescription: Subaru ECM has lost CAN communication with the vehicle.
fullDescription:
U1100 on Subaru indicates the ECM is not receiving or not sending valid CAN messages. Subaru platforms are prone to ground strap corrosion on the engine that causes this symptom.

Address grounds first, then check CAN pair integrity, before condemning the ECM.
safetyImpact: Engine may stall, ABS/stability disabled.

fixSteps.title: Clean engine grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean ground straps on engine/chassis; retorque to spec.

fixSteps.title: Verify CAN continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Check CAN pair continuity from ECM to DLC.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and reflash with Subaru SSMIV.

faq.q: Which ground strap is the common culprit?
faq.a: The engine-to-chassis strap near the intake manifold — inspect first.

title: Subaru - TCM CAN Communication Error
shortDescription: Subaru TCM has lost CAN communication.
fullDescription:
U1200 on Subaru indicates TCM CAN communication failure — the transmission can go into limp mode and the gear indicator may blank. On CVT-equipped Subarus, harness connectors on the TCM are a common failure point.

Inspect the TCM harness and connectors before replacing modules.
safetyImpact: Transmission in limp mode; reduced speed capability.

fixSteps.title: Inspect TCM connector
fixSteps.instruction: Remove TCM connector, check for corrosion, clean and reseat.

fixSteps.title: Check CAN continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Test CAN pair to TCM from DLC.

fixSteps.title: Replace TCM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and reflash via SSMIV.

faq.q: Does the CVT need relearning after TCM replacement?
faq.a: Yes — Subaru's CVT learn procedure must be run after any TCM replacement.

title: Communication Bus A Signal Invalid
shortDescription: Bus A is transmitting but signal content is invalid.
fullDescription:
U2012 sets when the primary (A) communication bus is electrically alive but the message content is not valid — wrong length, bad checksum, or unknown identifier. This points to a misconfigured or malfunctioning transmitter rather than a physical wiring fault.

Common root causes include a module with corrupted flash or a mismatched part number installed.
safetyImpact: Various module features may be disabled; no general drivability loss.

fixSteps.title: Identify offender
fixSteps.instruction: Scan all modules; the one reporting U2012 or the one silent is the target.

fixSteps.title: Reflash module
fixSteps.instruction: Flash to latest calibration with factory tool.

faq.q: Will clearing codes fix it?
faq.a: Only briefly — the code returns until the module is reflashed.

title: Control Module Configuration Not Programmed
shortDescription: A module is installed but has no valid configuration file.
fullDescription:
U2050 indicates a module has been installed without the required configuration data. The module is alive and on the bus but cannot operate until the correct configuration is programmed.

This is usually seen after replacing a module with a blank unit.
safetyImpact: The unconfigured module's features are disabled until programming is complete.

fixSteps.title: Program module
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory tool to load as-built configuration.

faq.q: Can independent shops program modules?
faq.a: Many can with J2534 pass-thru tools and factory subscriptions.

title: Initial CAN Bus Configuration Failure
shortDescription: Modules cannot agree on the initial CAN configuration on start-up.
fullDescription:
U2100 indicates the initial CAN handshake failed at key-on — modules could not enumerate or register with the gateway. The result is that no useful bus communication occurs.

This is typically a gateway module fault, a termination problem, or a severe wiring short.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may not start or run; widespread module failures.

fixSteps.title: Check DLC termination
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 60 ohms across CAN-H/CAN-L at the DLC.

fixSteps.title: Inspect gateway
fixSteps.instruction: Check gateway power, grounds, and connectors.

fixSteps.title: Replace gateway
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and program if gateway is confirmed bad.

faq.q: Is there a reset procedure?
faq.a: Many vehicles require a full power-down (battery disconnect 10+ minutes) to re-enumerate the bus.

title: Control Module Configuration Incompatible
shortDescription: Module configuration does not match expected vehicle options.
fullDescription:
U2102 sets when a module's stored configuration does not match the vehicle's option content as broadcast by the gateway. Example: a module flagged for AWD is installed in a 2WD vehicle.

Reprogram with correct as-built data to resolve.
safetyImpact: Affected features may behave incorrectly.

fixSteps.title: Verify part number
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm installed module part number matches VIN requirement.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram
fixSteps.instruction: Load correct as-built file.

faq.q: Will any module from a junkyard work?
faq.a: Only if part number matches and it supports reprogramming.

title: Control Module Configuration Incorrect Number of Modules
shortDescription: Gateway sees a different number of modules than expected.
fullDescription:
U2103 indicates the gateway's expected module count does not match actual modules on the bus — either extra or missing. After service (removal/addition) this is expected; otherwise it points to a module that has dropped off the bus.

Scan all modules, find the missing one, and restore communication.
safetyImpact: Features corresponding to missing modules are lost.

causes.cause: CAN wire broken to a module

fixSteps.title: Full scan
fixSteps.instruction: Run full-system scan to see which module is missing.

fixSteps.title: Restore comms
fixSteps.instruction: Check power, ground, and CAN wires for the missing module.

faq.q: Can I disable a module to stop this code?
faq.a: Only via as-built change; simply unplugging keeps the code set.

title: Control Module Software Incompatible
shortDescription: Module software version is not compatible with rest of vehicle.
fullDescription:
U2109 sets when a module's software version is below (or above) the level expected by the gateway. Common after installing a used module or after a partial flash that only updated some modules.

Resolve by flashing all relevant modules to their current TSB-recommended levels.
safetyImpact: Affected features may malfunction.

fixSteps.title: Pull software versions
fixSteps.instruction: Read software part numbers from each module.

fixSteps.title: Reflash
fixSteps.instruction: Flash to latest TSB-mandated calibration.

faq.q: Is reflashing safe?
faq.a: If done with good battery support and factory tools, yes — it's routine service.

title: Control Module Programming Incomplete
shortDescription: Module reflash process was interrupted.
fullDescription:
U2110 indicates the last programming session did not complete successfully. The module may be in recovery mode or have partial flash data. Retry the flash with good battery support (maintainer connected).

Do not drive the vehicle until the flash is completed — the module may be non-functional.
safetyImpact: Partially programmed module may cause multiple feature failures.

fixSteps.title: Connect battery maintainer
fixSteps.instruction: Attach a programming-grade maintainer (14V minimum).

fixSteps.title: Retry programming
fixSteps.instruction: Restart the flash session.

faq.q: Can a module be bricked?
faq.a: Rarely — most modern modules have recovery modes that survive a failed flash.

title: Control Module Configuration Data Invalid
shortDescription: Stored configuration data in module is corrupt.
fullDescription:
U2114 indicates the module's EEPROM or flash stores data that fails checksum validation. This can be caused by electrical disturbances, failing memory, or a previous bad flash.

Recover by reprogramming; if recurrent, replace the module.
safetyImpact: Module features disabled until recovered.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram
fixSteps.instruction: Reload as-built configuration.

fixSteps.title: Replace if recurrent
fixSteps.instruction: If the code returns within days, the memory is failing — replace the module.

faq.q: Can a voltage spike cause this?
faq.a: Yes — jump-starting with reversed polarity is a classic cause.

title: Restraint Control Module Configuration Fault
shortDescription: Airbag/SRS configuration is invalid.
fullDescription:
U2128 indicates the Restraint Control Module's configuration data is missing or invalid. SRS features including airbags and seatbelt pretensioners may be disabled for safety.

Must be corrected by factory-level programming before vehicle is considered safe to operate.
safetyImpact: Airbags may not deploy correctly in a crash.

fixSteps.title: Configure RCM
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory tool to write SRS as-built data.

faq.q: Can this be cleared with a generic tool?
faq.a: No — SRS programming requires manufacturer-specific security access.

title: Bus Communication with Instrument Cluster Lost
shortDescription: Cluster has dropped off the communication bus.
fullDescription:
U2149 indicates the instrument cluster is no longer responding on the network bus. Symptoms include blank gauges, no warning lamps, or mileage frozen at last value.

Causes include cluster power/ground issues, CAN wiring to cluster, or internal cluster fault.
safetyImpact: Driver loses speed, RPM, and warnings.

fixSteps.title: Check fuses
fixSteps.instruction: Verify cluster fuses are intact.

fixSteps.title: Test cluster
fixSteps.instruction: Check cluster power/ground and CAN.

fixSteps.title: Replace cluster
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and program cluster.

faq.q: Will a used cluster work?
faq.a: Yes, but mileage will show the donor's unless reprogrammed.

title: Invalid Data Received From Vehicle Speed Sensor
shortDescription: Speed sensor data on bus is implausible.
fullDescription:
U2184 indicates a module is receiving vehicle speed data that does not match expected bounds — either impossibly high, negative, or flatlined when the vehicle is moving. The source is typically the ABS module broadcasting wheel-speed-derived vehicle speed.

Check wheel speed sensors and ABS module first.
safetyImpact: Speedometer, cruise control, and ABS may be affected.

fixSteps.title: Check wheel speed sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Scan for ABS codes and replace failed sensor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ABS module
fixSteps.instruction: Test ABS module grounds and CAN connections.

faq.q: Does bad brakes cause this?
faq.a: No — but dirty tone rings that the sensor reads will cause erratic data.

title: Invalid Data Received From Engine Control Module
shortDescription: ECM broadcast data is outside valid range.
fullDescription:
U2192 indicates a receiving module is seeing implausible ECM data — RPM, torque request, coolant temp, or similar. Often accompanies other drivability faults.

Diagnose ECM power/ground and wiring before condemning the module.
safetyImpact: Other modules may derate performance based on bad data.

fixSteps.title: Test ECM grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Less than 0.1 ohm from ECM ground to battery negative.

fixSteps.title: Scope CAN
fixSteps.instruction: Look at CAN signal quality near ECM.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECM
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and reflash if confirmed internal fault.

faq.q: Is this always ECM's fault?
faq.a: No — bad grounds and CAN noise can make a good ECM look bad.

title: Invalid Data Received From Occupant Classification Module
shortDescription: OCS data for front passenger seat is implausible.
fullDescription:
U2198 indicates the Occupant Classification System (seat weight/pressure sensor) is sending data outside expected bounds. SRS module then cannot determine whether to enable the passenger airbag.

Liquid spills and physical damage to the seat mat are the most common causes.
safetyImpact: Passenger airbag may be disabled or deploy incorrectly.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate OCS
fixSteps.instruction: Run OCS calibration with empty seat and factory tool.

fixSteps.title: Replace seat mat
fixSteps.instruction: If calibration fails, replace the seat weight sensor mat.

faq.q: Can I disable the OCS?
faq.a: No — it's a federally mandated safety system.

title: Invalid Data Received From Steering Wheel Control Module
shortDescription: Steering wheel control module data implausible.
fullDescription:
U2202 indicates implausible data from the steering wheel control module (clockspring/SWCM) — typically button state or cruise request stuck on. The clockspring is a known wear item and a common cause.

Replacing the clockspring usually clears the code.
safetyImpact: Cruise control and steering-wheel buttons may malfunction; horn and airbag connections share the clockspring.

fixSteps.title: Test buttons
fixSteps.instruction: Scan live SWCM data while pressing each button.

fixSteps.title: Replace clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace clockspring — airbag must be disabled first.

faq.q: Do I need to recalibrate steering angle after clockspring?
faq.a: Usually yes — follow the factory centering procedure.

title: Invalid Data Received From Compass Module
shortDescription: Compass/heading data invalid on bus.
fullDescription:
U2224 indicates the compass module is sending invalid heading data. Minor issue; affects mirror-compass display and navigation dead reckoning only.

Calibration (figure-8 drive) typically fixes it; otherwise replace the mirror or sensor housing.
safetyImpact: Compass/navigation heading may be wrong; no safety impact.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate compass
fixSteps.instruction: Drive three figure-8 circles in an open area at low speed.

faq.q: Do I need to enter a compass zone?
faq.a: Most modern vehicles auto-detect; older ones require manual zone entry.

title: Invalid Data Received From Climate Control Module
shortDescription: HVAC module broadcast data is implausible.
fullDescription:
U2260 indicates the climate control module is sending invalid temperature or blower setpoint data. The code typically accompanies HVAC symptoms — no heat, no AC, or stuck blower.

Inspect the HVAC module and the sensors it reads (ambient, in-car temp, evap).
safetyImpact: Cabin comfort loss; defrost may not operate, reducing visibility.

fixSteps.title: Test sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Scan HVAC live data and verify sensor values are plausible.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the faulty input or the HVAC control module.

faq.q: Will defrost still work?
faq.a: Only if the module can still command the blend door; otherwise windows may fog.

title: Scan Tool Protocol Error
shortDescription: Scan tool-to-module handshake protocol error.
fullDescription:
U2410 indicates an error in the scan-tool-to-module diagnostic protocol — the scan tool sent a message the module could not parse, or vice versa. Typically seen with aftermarket tools lacking full protocol support.

Not a vehicle hardware fault; use a manufacturer-supported tool.
safetyImpact: None.

fixSteps.title: Update tool firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Apply latest updates to the scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Use OEM tool
fixSteps.instruction: If problem persists, use the manufacturer's scan tool.

faq.q: Will this clear itself?
faq.a: Usually yes — it only persists while a non-compliant tool is connected.

title: Diagnostic Session Terminated Unexpectedly
shortDescription: Diagnostic session dropped before completion.
fullDescription:
U2414 indicates a diagnostic session (often a flash or coding operation) ended abruptly. Usually caused by low voltage, tool disconnect, or ignition cycling during a session.

Retry the session with a battery maintainer connected.
safetyImpact: Depends on what was being programmed; partial flash may leave feature disabled.

fixSteps.title: Connect maintainer
fixSteps.instruction: Attach programming-grade battery maintainer.

fixSteps.title: Retry session
fixSteps.instruction: Restart programming and do not disturb until complete.

faq.q: Can I recover from bricked module?
faq.a: Most modules have recovery modes; consult factory procedure.

title: CAN Network Reconfiguration Required
shortDescription: Gateway requires network reconfiguration after module change.
fullDescription:
U2500 sets when the gateway detects a network topology change (module added or removed) that requires a reconfiguration sweep. Until completed, some modules may not be visible.

Run the factory network configuration routine to resolve.
safetyImpact: Affected module features unavailable until reconfiguration completes.

fixSteps.title: Run reconfiguration
fixSteps.instruction: Factory tool offers a network reconfiguration routine — run it.

faq.q: Is this the same as 'marry to VIN'?
faq.a: It's one step of that process — the gateway needs to know the new module exists.

title: Lost Communication With Hybrid Battery Pack
shortDescription: HV battery pack is not communicating with the hybrid controller.
fullDescription:
U029F indicates loss of communication between the hybrid/EV battery pack and the HV controller (typically via a dedicated internal HV CAN). This disables the hybrid system and the vehicle enters reduced-power or ICE-only mode.

Start diagnosis at the HV battery service disconnect and its CAN harness; moisture and vibration are common enemies.
safetyImpact: Hybrid functions lost; vehicle may not be drivable on EV power.

fixSteps.title: Safe isolation first
fixSteps.instruction: Observe HV safety procedures — remove service disconnect and wait per manufacturer before any work.

fixSteps.title: Inspect HV CAN harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check the CAN pair between battery pack and HV controller.

fixSteps.title: Reseat or replace BMS
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat connectors; if internal BMS fault, replace pack BMS.

faq.q: Can I DIY hybrid battery work?
faq.a: Not recommended — high voltage is lethal; leave to trained technicians.

title: HV Battery Cell Voltage Sensor 1 Comm Fault
shortDescription: Hybrid battery cell voltage sensor circuit 1 not communicating.
fullDescription:
U02A0 indicates the BMS cannot read cell voltage data from sensor group 1. Without cell-level voltage data the BMS cannot balance or protect the pack and will derate or disable the hybrid system.

Causes include a failing CMU (cell monitoring unit), wiring harness in the pack, or water intrusion.
safetyImpact: Hybrid system disabled; pack may be at risk if fault persists.

fixSteps.title: HV safe work
fixSteps.instruction: Follow HV safety procedures before opening pack.

fixSteps.title: Replace CMU
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the specific cell monitoring unit.

faq.q: Will the vehicle still drive?
faq.a: Often in limp mode — power is severely limited.

title: HV Battery Cell Voltage Sensor 2 Comm Fault
shortDescription: Hybrid battery cell voltage sensor circuit 2 not communicating.
fullDescription: U02A1 mirrors U02A0 but for cell sensor group 2. Symptoms and repair path are identical — BMS loses partial visibility into the pack and derates hybrid operation.
safetyImpact: Hybrid system disabled; pack protection reduced.

fixSteps.title: HV safety
fixSteps.instruction: Follow HV work procedures.

fixSteps.title: Replace CMU 2
fixSteps.instruction: Swap cell monitoring unit 2.

faq.q: Can I run the pack without this sensor?
faq.a: No — safety logic refuses to operate without full visibility.

title: HV Battery Temperature Sensor Comm Fault
shortDescription: Hybrid battery temperature sensor not communicating.
fullDescription:
U02A2 indicates loss of battery temperature data. Temperature is critical for charge/discharge rate limits and cell balancing; without it the BMS forces a conservative derate or shuts the pack down.

Inspect the thermistor harness in the pack and the connector to the BMS.
safetyImpact: Hybrid power severely limited.
symptoms: Battery temp reads invalid on scan tool

fixSteps.title: HV safety
fixSteps.instruction: Follow HV procedures.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap faulty thermistor or repair harness.

faq.q: Is this a fire risk?
faq.a: Loss of temp monitoring is why the BMS derates — the system is protecting itself.

title: Hybrid Vehicle CAN Comm Master Fault
shortDescription: Hybrid-specific CAN master fault across multiple HV modules.
fullDescription:
U1000 on several hybrid platforms (Toyota THS, Honda IMA/i-MMD) is the master 'multiple CAN malfunction' code. When any subordinate HV module loses comms, the HV controller posts U1000 in parallel with the specific sub-code.

The U1000 itself is not diagnostic — the accompanying sub-codes point to the actual fault.
safetyImpact: Full hybrid disable; vehicle may refuse to shift READY.

fixSteps.title: Diagnose sub-codes
fixSteps.instruction: Address each sub-code individually — U1000 self-clears when they are fixed.

faq.q: Can I clear U1000 alone?
faq.a: It will return immediately — treat sub-codes first.

title: Inverter/Converter CAN Communication Fault
shortDescription: Traction inverter/converter not communicating with HV controller.
fullDescription:
U2300 indicates the inverter/converter assembly (which steps HV DC to three-phase AC for the traction motor) has lost or is sending invalid CAN data. The hybrid system cannot safely drive the motor and disables propulsion assist.

Inverter faults often follow coolant loss or water intrusion.
safetyImpact: Loss of EV drive and regenerative braking.

fixSteps.title: Check inverter coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Verify inverter coolant level and pump operation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect HV CAN
fixSteps.instruction: Test CAN pair between inverter and HV controller.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace if confirmed bad; very expensive.

faq.q: Why is this so expensive?
faq.a: Inverters are high-power assemblies and are a dealer-replaced item on most hybrids.

title: Invalid Data Received From Steering Angle Sensor
shortDescription: Steering angle sensor data is implausible.
fullDescription:
U0428 indicates the steering angle sensor is reporting data that does not make sense — e.g., unchanging while the vehicle is turning. ESP, lane-keep, and adaptive cruise depend on this signal; they will be disabled until resolved.

Fixes include recalibration or replacement of the clockspring-integrated sensor.
safetyImpact: Stability control, lane-keep, and adaptive cruise disabled.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Run factory zero-point calibration with front wheels straight.

fixSteps.title: Replace clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: If calibration fails, replace clockspring/SAS assembly.

faq.q: Do I need calibration after alignment?
faq.a: Yes — any steering work requires SAS zero-point reset.

title: Invalid Data Received From Tire Pressure Monitor
shortDescription: Tire pressure monitor broadcast data is implausible.
fullDescription:
U0429 indicates TPMS is sending out-of-range pressure or ID data. The cluster may show dashes or wrong-position warnings. Sensors with low batteries or damaged antenna are common causes.

Replace failing sensors and relearn the system.
safetyImpact: TPMS monitoring effectively disabled; risk of undetected low tire.

fixSteps.title: Read sensor status
fixSteps.instruction: Use TPMS tool to check each sensor's battery and response.

fixSteps.title: Replace weak sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and relearn.

faq.q: How long do TPMS sensor batteries last?
faq.a: Typically 7-10 years, shorter with high-mileage highway use.

title: Invalid Data Received From Immobilizer Control Module
shortDescription: Immobilizer data is implausible on bus.
fullDescription:
U0431 is similar to U0801 but set by a different receiving module. The PCM cannot validate the immobilizer message, leading to engine-start prevention or stall after start.

Check antenna ring, keys, and immobilizer module.
safetyImpact: No-start or stall.

fixSteps.title: Try spare key
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fob vs antenna by using spare.

fixSteps.title: Inspect antenna
fixSteps.instruction: Check antenna connector at steering lock.

fixSteps.title: Replace module/antenna
fixSteps.instruction: Replace faulty component; program keys.

faq.q: Could a phone in my pocket interfere?
faq.a: Rarely — but strong RF sources can cause intermittent read failures.

title: Invalid Data Received From Adaptive Headlight Module
shortDescription: Adaptive headlight module data is implausible.
fullDescription:
U0434 indicates the adaptive headlight control module is sending invalid data — beam position, turn angle, or auto-leveling. AFS/AHB features are disabled and lights default to static beam.

Causes are typically headlight leveling motor faults or module internal defects.
safetyImpact: Night-time visibility reduced; beam steering lost.

fixSteps.title: Command motors
fixSteps.instruction: Bidirectional command the leveling motors; note non-responders.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor/module
fixSteps.instruction: Replace faulty motor or headlight control module.

faq.q: Will the MIL come on?
faq.a: Usually no — AFS-only light comes on in the cluster.

title: Invalid Data Received From Rain Sensor Module
shortDescription: Rain sensor data is out of range.
fullDescription:
U0449 indicates the rain/light sensor behind the windshield is reporting invalid data. Automatic wipers, auto-headlights, and auto-dim mirrors lose input.

The sensor is commonly gel-bonded to the glass; replacement of the gel pad or sensor usually solves it.
safetyImpact: Auto-wipers and auto-headlights inoperative.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor area
fixSteps.instruction: Clean glass behind sensor and sensor lens.

fixSteps.title: Replace gel pad
fixSteps.instruction: Detach sensor, install fresh gel pad.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new rain/light sensor.

faq.q: Do I need calibration?
faq.a: Some vehicles require a short learning drive; others are plug-and-play.

title: Invalid Data Received From Hybrid Battery Pack
shortDescription: Hybrid battery pack broadcast data out of range.
fullDescription:
U0451 indicates a receiving module is getting implausible data from the HV battery pack — state-of-charge jumps, impossible voltages, or wrong IDs. Accompanies other HV codes and indicates BMS or harness issues.

Diagnose with HV safety procedures.
safetyImpact: Hybrid system disabled.

fixSteps.title: HV safe isolation
fixSteps.instruction: Remove service plug and wait.

fixSteps.title: Replace BMS
fixSteps.instruction: Swap battery management module.

faq.q: Is a third-party BMS safe?
faq.a: Use OEM or OEM-equivalent; the BMS is safety-critical.

title: Invalid Data Received From Hybrid Battery Monitor
shortDescription: Hybrid battery monitor (sub-module) data implausible.
fullDescription:
U0452 indicates the battery monitor — a sub-module reporting current, voltage, and temperature to the BMS — is sending invalid data. Result is reduced or disabled hybrid operation.

Often fixed by replacing the current/voltage sense module or its harness.
safetyImpact: Hybrid operation severely limited.

fixSteps.title: HV safety
fixSteps.instruction: Follow HV procedures.

fixSteps.title: Replace monitor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap battery monitor module; reseat HV connections.

faq.q: Can a low 12V battery cause this?
faq.a: Yes on some hybrids — weak aux 12V can make the monitor boot unreliably.

title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus (+)
shortDescription: Fault detected on the high speed CAN bus positive line.
fullDescription:
U0005 indicates that a control module has detected a fault on the high-speed CAN bus positive (CAN+) line. This is a generic bus wiring code that points to a short, open, or high-resistance fault on CAN High rather than a specific module loss.

Symptoms often include multiple warning lights, loss of communication DTCs from many modules, and limp-home operation. Because the entire vehicle network depends on CAN High integrity, the problem is usually electrical (harness, connector) rather than module-level.
safetyImpact: Widespread loss of functions including ABS, traction control, and instrument cluster reporting.

causes.cause: Short to ground on CAN High wire
Damaged bus connector or corroded pin

fixSteps.title: Scan all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Read DTCs from every reachable module to identify which are still on the bus.

fixSteps.title: Measure bus resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With ignition off, measure resistance across CAN High/Low at the DLC; should be ~60 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check CAN High wire for shorts to ground/power and for broken insulation.

faq.q: Is U0005 the same as U0001?
faq.a: U0001 is generic CAN failure; U0005 narrows it to the CAN High line.

title: High Speed CAN Communication Bus Shorted to Bus (-)
shortDescription: High-speed CAN High wire is shorted to CAN Low.
fullDescription:
U0009 is set when the powertrain network diagnostic detects that the CAN High line is shorted to the CAN Low line, collapsing the differential signal. The bus can no longer carry data, so many modules will time out.

This is almost always a wiring fault — pinched harness, water intrusion in a connector, or a repair splice with damaged insulation. Less often, an internal module fault can pull the two lines together.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may enter fail-safe mode; ABS, stability, and cluster gauges may stop working.

causes.cause: Harness pinch or chafe shorting CAN+ to CAN-
Water intrusion into a bus connector

fixSteps.title: Check for shorts
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery, measure resistance between CAN High and CAN Low with all modules connected then progressively disconnected.

fixSteps.title: Locate pinch point
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect bus harness along the chassis for damage; check areas near firewall and door jambs.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace damaged section with twisted-pair CAN wire and solder/heat-shrink splice.

faq.q: Can I clear this without finding the short?
faq.a: No — the code will set again within seconds of key-on.

title: Medium Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Open
shortDescription: Open circuit detected on medium speed CAN High line.
fullDescription:
U0013 indicates an open circuit on the medium-speed CAN High line, commonly used for body and comfort modules. The affected sub-network cannot transmit, so body functions (doors, windows, lights) may stop responding.

Opens typically occur at connectors or splice points rather than in wire runs. A break in CAN High disables half the differential pair and causes mass communication loss across modules on that segment.
safetyImpact: Body system features lost; critical systems usually continue to operate.

causes.cause: Disconnected module pulling bus segment offline

fixSteps.title: Identify bus segment
fixSteps.instruction: Use a wiring diagram to find which modules live on medium-speed CAN.

fixSteps.title: Ring-out CAN High
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity of CAN+ from end to end of the segment.

fixSteps.title: Repair open
fixSteps.instruction: Repair broken wire or re-pin the connector.

faq.q: Will the engine still run?
faq.a: Yes, the engine runs on high-speed CAN — medium speed only affects body comfort systems.

title: Low Speed CAN Communication Bus
shortDescription: Fault detected on low-speed CAN communication bus.
fullDescription:
U0020 indicates a generic fault on the low-speed CAN bus. Low-speed CAN (often called LS-CAN or Single-Wire CAN on GM vehicles) handles non-time-critical data like HVAC, radio, and diagnostic requests.

A fault here typically affects convenience features. The cause is usually wiring-related: a short, open, or a failed module dragging the single-wire bus out of its normal recessive voltage.
safetyImpact: Minimal — affects convenience features, not driving controls.

causes.cause: Short to ground on single-wire CAN
Failed radio, HVAC, or body module

symptoms: Scan tool can't reach some modules

fixSteps.title: Read DTCs from all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Identify which low-speed CAN modules are offline.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect modules one at a time
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug each LS-CAN module to see if the bus recovers.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring or replace module
fixSteps.instruction: Fix found fault based on step 2 results.

faq.q: Is low-speed CAN the same as LIN?
faq.a: No — LIN is a separate slower single-master bus; low-speed CAN still uses CAN protocol at lower baud rate.

title: Low Speed CAN Communication Bus (+) Open
shortDescription: Open detected on low-speed CAN High line.
fullDescription:
U0022 sets when the low-speed CAN High line is open. Without a path for the positive differential line, the whole low-speed segment cannot communicate. Convenience modules (radio, HVAC, seat, mirror) may go silent.

Typical cause is a broken wire near a connector or a pulled terminal. Because low-speed CAN often uses shared splice packs, one corroded splice can take out several modules.
safetyImpact: Low — comfort features only.

causes.cause: Loose or backed-out pin in connector

fixSteps.title: Locate splice pack
fixSteps.instruction: Find the LS-CAN splice pack in the wiring diagram and inspect it.

fixSteps.title: Continuity test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify CAN+ continuity from splice to each module.

fixSteps.title: Repair open
fixSteps.instruction: Solder or re-pin as needed.

faq.q: Will the engine run?
faq.a: Yes, engine modules use a different bus.

title: Low Speed CAN Communication Bus (-) Shorted to Battery
shortDescription: Low-speed CAN Low line is shorted to battery voltage.
fullDescription:
U0025 is logged when CAN Low on the low-speed bus is pulled up to battery voltage. Normal CAN Low idles near 0V (or 5V recessive on LS-CAN), so a short to B+ destroys bus signaling.

Common causes include a chafed harness against a power wire, water intrusion in a fusebox bridging pins, or a failed module with an internal short. The short may also damage transceiver ICs in attached modules.
safetyImpact: Convenience features lost; possible module transceiver damage.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect battery
fixSteps.instruction: Remove negative terminal before working on a B+ short.

fixSteps.title: Measure short voltage
fixSteps.instruction: With key on, probe CAN- for voltage; >1V indicates a short source.

fixSteps.title: Isolate source
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug modules one at a time to find the one feeding B+ onto the bus.

faq.q: Can this damage other modules?
faq.a: Yes — prolonged B+ on CAN can destroy transceivers in connected ECUs.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus C
shortDescription: Generic fault on vehicle communication bus C.
fullDescription:
U0030 is a generic SAE code that reports a failure on Bus C of the vehicle communication network. Manufacturers may assign Bus C to chassis, body, or infotainment domains depending on the platform.

Diagnosis starts with consulting the vehicle-specific wiring diagram to determine which modules belong to Bus C, then ring-out for shorts, opens, and resistance issues.
safetyImpact: Depends on which domain Bus C covers on the specific vehicle.

causes.cause: Wiring short or open on Bus C

symptoms: Loss of features tied to Bus C

fixSteps.title: Identify Bus C modules
fixSteps.instruction: Look up which modules are on Bus C for this make/model.

fixSteps.title: Test bus integrity
fixSteps.instruction: Check resistance and inspect harness.

fixSteps.title: Repair as needed
fixSteps.instruction: Fix wiring or replace faulted module.

faq.q: Which bus is Bus C?
faq.a: There is no universal answer — it varies per manufacturer.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus C (+) Low
shortDescription: Bus C positive line voltage is too low.
fullDescription:
U0032 reports that the voltage on Bus C CAN High is below the valid threshold. A common reason is a short to ground that is intermittent or partial (high-resistance short).

Start with harness inspection at the most frequently damaged areas (trunk hinges, door jambs, firewall) and then measure CAN High to ground with the bus powered.
safetyImpact: Bus C features degraded or lost.

causes.cause: High-resistance short to ground on CAN+

fixSteps.title: Voltage check
fixSteps.instruction: Measure CAN+ voltage with key on — should be ~2.5V idle rising to ~3.5V dominant.

fixSteps.title: Flex test harness
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle harness while scoping bus to reveal intermittents.

faq.q: Do I need a scope?
faq.a: Helpful but not required — a DMM with MIN/MAX can catch dips too.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus D (-) Shorted to Bus (-)
shortDescription: Bus D CAN Low shorted to another CAN Low circuit.
fullDescription:
U0044 indicates that Bus D CAN Low is electrically tied to another bus's CAN Low line. On multi-bus vehicles, gateways separate networks and mixing buses corrupts both. This can happen after an improper repair or a rodent-chewed harness.

The fix requires tracing the illegal splice and restoring proper isolation.
safetyImpact: Two network segments affected; various features lost.

fixSteps.title: Review prior repairs
fixSteps.instruction: Check for recent harness work that might have tied buses together.

fixSteps.title: Isolate buses
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect gateway module and test continuity between the two CAN- lines.

faq.q: Will disconnecting the gateway clear the code?
faq.a: It may, but the underlying short still needs repair.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus E (-) Shorted to Battery
shortDescription: Bus E CAN Low shorted to battery voltage.
fullDescription:
U0055 sets when Bus E CAN Low is pulled up to battery voltage. Bus E designations vary by platform but often cover infotainment or driver-assistance networks. The short damages signaling and may harm module transceivers.

Disconnect the battery before probing, then isolate the source by unplugging modules until the short disappears.
safetyImpact: Features on Bus E lost; potential transceiver damage.

fixSteps.title: Battery off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect battery before probing.

fixSteps.title: Isolate short
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug Bus E modules one by one to find source.

fixSteps.title: Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Fix chafed wire or replace failed module.

faq.q: Can this ruin modules?
faq.a: Yes — prolonged short to B+ kills CAN transceivers.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus F Performance
shortDescription: Performance problem on vehicle communication Bus F.
fullDescription:
U0069 flags a performance-level fault on Bus F — communication is present but corrupted, slow, or producing CRC errors. This is distinct from a flat open or short: the bus partially works.

Common causes are marginal terminating resistors, a failing transceiver IC, or EMI from a faulty aftermarket device. Start with bus load and resistance measurements.
safetyImpact: Intermittent feature loss, possibly worsening over time.

fixSteps.title: Measure terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Resistance should be ~60 ohms across CAN+/- at the DLC.

fixSteps.title: Scope bus traffic
fixSteps.instruction: Look for malformed frames and excessive error frames.

faq.q: What is bus performance?
faq.a: It means data is present but not meeting protocol timing/quality.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus B Off — Restraints CAN
shortDescription: Restraints CAN sub-bus has gone bus-off.
fullDescription:
On some GM and Stellantis platforms, U0077 is applied to the dedicated restraints CAN segment. When the restraints controller takes itself off the bus due to excessive error frames, airbag readiness lights illuminate and SRS may be disabled.

Causes are typically wiring issues at the steering column clockspring, under-seat harness pinches, or a failing SRS module.
safetyImpact: Airbags may be disabled; SRS light on.

fixSteps.title: Disable SRS
fixSteps.instruction: Follow manufacturer procedure to safely disable airbags before probing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look under seats and at clockspring for damage.

fixSteps.title: Test SRS module
fixSteps.instruction: Verify module power/ground and replace if internal fault.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive?
faq.a: No — airbags may not deploy in a crash.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus G (+) Open
shortDescription: Open circuit on Bus G CAN High line.
fullDescription:
U0082 indicates Bus G CAN High has an open circuit. Bus G assignments vary, but this segment is often used for chassis or driver assistance modules on premium vehicles.

Inspect splice packs and connector pins. Bus G segments with only two or three modules are particularly sensitive because an open at either end effectively disables the entire bus.
safetyImpact: Chassis/ADAS features on Bus G lost.

fixSteps.title: Map Bus G
fixSteps.instruction: Identify Bus G modules and wiring topology for this vehicle.

fixSteps.title: Ring out CAN+
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity end to end.

faq.q: Where is Bus G?
faq.a: Check the wiring diagram — it is platform-specific.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus G (-) Low
shortDescription: Bus G CAN Low voltage too low.
fullDescription:
U0087 sets when the voltage on Bus G CAN Low drops below threshold. A high-resistance short to ground or a failing transceiver pulling the line below normal recessive can trigger this.

Pinpoint with a scope; intermittent faults often only show under certain thermal or vibration conditions.
safetyImpact: Bus G features intermittent or lost.

fixSteps.title: Scope capture
fixSteps.instruction: Record bus waveform during the fault condition.

fixSteps.title: Isolate
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug Bus G modules to find the one dragging the line.

faq.q: Can I drive with U0087?
faq.a: Yes, but ADAS reliability may be compromised.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus G (-) High
shortDescription: Bus G CAN Low voltage too high.
fullDescription:
U0088 indicates Bus G CAN Low is stuck above its allowed range. Often caused by a short to battery or module regulator failure that raises the reference.

If left uncorrected, the elevated voltage can stress transceivers across the segment.
safetyImpact: Loss of Bus G features; potential module damage.

fixSteps.title: Battery off
fixSteps.instruction: Remove power before probing a B+ short.

fixSteps.title: Find source
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug modules one at a time.

faq.q: Is module damage likely?
faq.a: Possible if the short persists for extended time.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus H Off
shortDescription: Bus H has entered bus-off state.
fullDescription:
U0095 reports that Bus H has gone bus-off. CAN controllers enter bus-off after exceeding an error counter threshold (TEC > 255), meaning the node has disabled itself to protect the network.

Look for wiring faults, rapid error bursts from a single module, or severe EMI. The problem usually returns instantly after a clear if not fixed.
safetyImpact: Depends on Bus H assignment; can be significant.
symptoms: Features tied to Bus H inoperative

fixSteps.title: Check termination
fixSteps.instruction: Measure ~60 ohms across Bus H CAN+/-.

fixSteps.title: Scope for error frames
fixSteps.instruction: Look for which node is producing the errors.

faq.q: Will clearing fix it?
faq.a: Only if the fault condition is gone; usually it returns immediately.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus H Performance
shortDescription: Performance fault on Bus H.
fullDescription:
U0099 indicates a performance issue on Bus H — marginal signaling, excessive error frames, or bus load out of normal range. Unlike U0095 (bus-off), the bus is still working partially.

Inspect resistors, transceivers, and any aftermarket devices tapped into Bus H.
safetyImpact: Intermittent feature loss.

fixSteps.title: Remove aftermarket devices
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily disconnect any non-OEM modules.

fixSteps.title: Scope bus
fixSteps.instruction: Look for malformed frames under load.

faq.q: Can aftermarket alarms cause this?
faq.a: Yes — poorly designed alarms and remote starts are frequent offenders.

title: Lost Communication with Restraints Control Module
shortDescription: Communication with the airbag/restraints control module lost.
fullDescription:
U0151 is set by other modules when they stop receiving expected messages from the Restraints Control Module (RCM/SRS/ORC). Because the RCM is responsible for airbag and pretensioner deployment, loss of communication immediately disables crash protection.

The root cause is usually a blown SRS fuse, failed RCM, or a bus fault on the segment the RCM shares with the rest of the vehicle.
safetyImpact: Airbags and pretensioners may not deploy in a crash.
symptoms: SRS module not responding on scan tool

fixSteps.title: Check SRS fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the airbag/SRS fuse is intact.

fixSteps.title: Verify RCM power/ground
fixSteps.instruction: Measure B+ and ground at the RCM connector per wiring diagram.

fixSteps.title: Replace RCM if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If power/ground/CAN are fine, replace the RCM; follow SRS safety procedures.

faq.q: Does a flooded RCM cause this?
faq.a: Yes — water damage commonly kills RCMs located under carpet.

title: Lost Communication with Navigation Display Module
shortDescription: Navigation display module is not communicating.
fullDescription:
U0158 sets when the vehicle network cannot reach the navigation display module. The map/infotainment screen may freeze, reboot, or stay black.

Check power/ground and the infotainment sub-bus. A disconnected antenna does not cause U0158 — this is specifically a communication loss with the display unit itself.
safetyImpact: Low — navigation lost, driving controls unaffected.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse/power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify infotainment fuse and B+ at the head unit.

fixSteps.title: Test CAN at head unit
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm bus traffic present at the nav connector.

faq.q: Will the radio still work?
faq.a: On vehicles with separate radio/nav modules, yes.

title: Lost Communication with Lane Departure Warning Camera
shortDescription: Lane departure/lane keep camera not communicating.
fullDescription:
U0163 is set when the forward-facing camera (used for lane departure, lane keep assist, and sometimes adaptive cruise) stops communicating on the ADAS bus. Lane assist features will be disabled.

Common causes include a cracked or foggy windshield blocking the camera, a disturbed camera mount after glass replacement, or a failed camera module.
safetyImpact: Lane keep assist and some ADAS features disabled.

fixSteps.title: Check camera view
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm nothing obstructs the camera lens behind the mirror.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check power, ground, and CAN at camera connector.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate or replace
fixSteps.instruction: If camera is faulty, replace and perform dynamic/static calibration.

faq.q: Does a new windshield require calibration?
faq.a: Yes — almost always, otherwise this code returns.

title: Lost Communication with HVAC Control Module
shortDescription: HVAC control module not communicating.
fullDescription:
U0164 sets when the vehicle network loses communication with the HVAC (climate control) module. The climate display may freeze, blower may stop, or defaults may engage.

Most often a connector or power issue at the HVAC module, especially after work on the dash. Water intrusion from a plugged evaporator drain can also kill the module.
safetyImpact: Low — comfort feature only, but defrost loss can impair visibility.

causes.cause: Water damage from plugged AC drain

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and reseat HVAC module connectors.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Verify HVAC fuse is intact.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for water
fixSteps.instruction: Check carpet under HVAC for moisture indicating blocked drain.

faq.q: Can defrost failure be safety relevant?
faq.a: Yes — loss of defrost in winter reduces visibility.

title: Lost Communication with Remote Function Actuation Module
shortDescription: RFA/RKE module not communicating.
fullDescription:
U0178 indicates lost communication with the Remote Function Actuator — the module that handles keyless entry, remote start, and sometimes passive entry. When offline, the fob may not lock/unlock and remote start will fail.

Common causes are a blown fuse, water intrusion to the RFA module, or a bus issue on the body segment.
safetyImpact: Low — security/convenience feature only.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Verify RFA fuse in the BCM/fuse box.

fixSteps.title: Test module power
fixSteps.instruction: Verify B+ and ground at RFA connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace if dead
fixSteps.instruction: Replace and program the RFA module if faulty.

faq.q: Will the car still start?
faq.a: If using the mechanical key/push-start, usually yes, but passive entry may need the fob held to the start button.

title: Invalid Data Received from Hybrid Battery Cell Monitor A
shortDescription: Battery cell monitor A reporting invalid cell data.
fullDescription:
U02A0 sets when the hybrid battery management system receives implausible cell voltage data from cell monitor A. Each monitor IC oversees a block of cells; if its reports contradict other monitors or exceed physical bounds, the BMS flags this code.

Causes range from a failed monitor IC to loose cell voltage sense wires. Continuing to drive risks cell overcharge or undervoltage because the BMS cannot trust balancing commands.
safetyImpact: Hybrid battery may derate or disable propulsion; fire risk if cells run uncontrolled.

causes.cause: Failed cell monitor IC on block A

fixSteps.title: HV safety lockout
fixSteps.instruction: Follow OEM HV safety procedure before opening the pack.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sense wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check cell sense harness to monitor A for loose or broken wires.

fixSteps.title: Replace monitor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace cell monitor IC board if harness is good.

faq.q: Can I DIY this?
faq.a: Only if you are HV-certified. This work involves lethal voltages.

title: Invalid Data Received from Hybrid Battery Cell Monitor B
shortDescription: Battery cell monitor B reporting invalid cell data.
fullDescription:
U02A1 behaves like U02A0 but for monitor B, overseeing a different block of cells. Multiple monitor codes together strongly suggest a shared wiring harness or BMS controller issue rather than two coincident IC failures.

Diagnose via the service tool's live cell voltage view; invalid or frozen readings pinpoint which monitor is at fault.
safetyImpact: Battery derate, reduced propulsion; HV safety risk.

causes.cause: Failed cell monitor IC on block B

fixSteps.title: Check live data
fixSteps.instruction: View cell voltages to identify which block reports invalid data.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Trace the sense harness to monitor B for damage.

faq.q: Does this affect warranty?
faq.a: Hybrid batteries often have extended federal warranty — check before paying out of pocket.

title: Invalid Data Received from Fuel Cell Management Module
shortDescription: Fuel cell management module reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
U02A5 is set on hydrogen fuel cell vehicles when the fuel cell management module transmits data that fails the vehicle controller's plausibility checks. The fuel cell stack may be shut down until the fault clears.

Causes include failed stack sensors, coolant conductivity issues, or a failed fuel cell ECU. Hydrogen systems require specialized training; consult manufacturer service information.
safetyImpact: Propulsion lost; potential hydrogen leak if sensor integrity compromised.

causes.cause: Failed stack temperature or voltage sensor
Fuel cell control ECU internal fault

fixSteps.title: OEM scan tool
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve detailed FC stack data via the manufacturer tool.

fixSteps.title: Check coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Verify FC coolant conductivity is within spec.

faq.q: Which cars have this?
faq.a: Toyota Mirai, Hyundai Nexo, Honda Clarity FCEV.

title: Invalid Data Received from Transmission Control Module A
shortDescription: Primary TCM is reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
U0728 sets when another module (often the ECM or gateway) receives data from Transmission Control Module A that fails plausibility or CRC checks. The TCM may still be on the bus, but the messages it sends are malformed or contradictory.

Look for software mismatch after a recent reflash, grounding issues at the TCM, or transceiver degradation.
safetyImpact: Transmission may enter limp mode.

fixSteps.title: Check software level
fixSteps.instruction: Verify TCM has the latest calibration from the manufacturer.

fixSteps.title: Clean grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Clean and tighten TCM ground points.

faq.q: What is 'Module A'?
faq.a: On vehicles with multiple TCMs (e.g., dual-clutch), 'A' is the primary controller.

title: Invalid Data Received from Transmission Control Module B
shortDescription: Secondary TCM is reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
U0729 mirrors U0728 but applies to TCM B — often the secondary controller on dual-clutch or tandem transmission systems. The two TCMs coordinate clutch engagement and shift scheduling; invalid data from one breaks that coordination.

Update software, check TCM B power/ground and bus wiring.
safetyImpact: Dual-clutch misbehavior, limp mode.

causes.cause: TCM B software out of date

symptoms: Won't shift into second clutch gears

fixSteps.title: Reflash TCM B
fixSteps.instruction: Apply latest calibration via OEM tool.

fixSteps.title: Verify power/ground
fixSteps.instruction: Check TCM B power and ground integrity.

faq.q: Is TCM B always present?
faq.a: Only on certain DCT and tandem transmission designs.

title: Invalid Data Received from Transmission Control Module C
shortDescription: Tertiary TCM is reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
U0730 applies where a third transmission controller exists (some commercial trucks, heavy-duty applications, or certain hybrid transmissions with motor-generator controllers classified as TCM C). Invalid data from this controller causes shift coordination faults.

Diagnosis steps mirror U0728/U0729 but target TCM C.
safetyImpact: Shift issues or limp mode.

fixSteps.title: Verify TCM C presence
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the vehicle has a TCM C per service info.

fixSteps.title: Software/power check
fixSteps.instruction: Update software and verify power/ground.

faq.q: Which vehicles have TCM C?
faq.a: Some heavy-duty and hybrid applications — not typical on passenger cars.

title: Invalid Data Received from Clutch A Control Module
shortDescription: Clutch A controller reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
U0901 indicates that data from Clutch A control module (odd-gear clutch on many DCTs) fails validation. Clutch engagement may be compromised, producing shudder or refusing to engage gears served by that clutch.

Inspect clutch position sensor wiring and software level of the clutch controller.
safetyImpact: Potential loss of drive gears served by clutch A.

fixSteps.title: Read clutch data
fixSteps.instruction: Observe clutch A position vs command in live data.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check clutch position sensor and harness.

faq.q: Is clutch replacement needed?
faq.a: Not necessarily — this is a data/electrical code, not wear-based.

title: Invalid Data Received from Clutch B Control Module
shortDescription: Clutch B controller reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
U0902 is the even-gear counterpart to U0901 on DCT transmissions. Clutch B handles the opposite gearset; invalid data here disrupts the DCT's handoff between clutches during shifts.

Check clutch B sensors, actuator wiring, and controller software as with U0901.
safetyImpact: Loss of even gears possible.

fixSteps.title: Live data check
fixSteps.instruction: Observe clutch B engagement patterns.

fixSteps.title: Sensor/harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect clutch B wiring.

faq.q: Can this be a sensor recall?
faq.a: Some VW/Ford DCTs have had position sensor recalls — check your VIN.

title: Invalid Data Received from High Voltage Charge Control Module
shortDescription: HV charge control module reporting invalid data.
fullDescription:
