U0915 is set when the HV charge controller (onboard charger / DC-DC interface module) sends implausible data to the vehicle. Charging may be blocked or limited to reduced rate for safety.

This is common after firmware updates, water intrusion into the charge port area, or internal module faults. Diagnostic access normally requires the OEM tool.
safetyImpact: Charging disabled or derated; vehicle cannot be fully charged.

fixSteps.title: OEM scan
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve specific sub-codes from the charge controller.

fixSteps.title: Inspect charge port
fixSteps.instruction: Look for moisture, debris, or damaged pins.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Apply TSB firmware or replace the onboard charger.

faq.q: Can I use DC fast charging?
faq.a: Sometimes AC charging is blocked but DCFC still works; check with OEM tool.

title: Manufacturer - Transmission Control Module Communication Malfunction
shortDescription: Manufacturer-specific TCM network fault (U1701).
fullDescription:
U1701 is a manufacturer-specific code indicating the powertrain or body control module has lost or received corrupted communication frames from the transmission control module on the manufacturer-proprietary subnet.

This code is commonly seen on older Ford and GM platforms that used pre-CAN class-2 buses (SCP, J1850-VPW). It can also appear on newer vehicles after a TCM replacement without programming.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Check battery & grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 12V battery voltage >12.4V and clean all chassis/engine grounds. Low voltage is the #1 cause of spurious U-codes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect TCM harness
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug TCM and check for bent/green pins and water intrusion.

fixSteps.title: Measure bus
fixSteps.instruction: Check bus voltage at TCM connector per factory spec.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: Will a new TCM fix it?
faq.a: Only if programmed to the VIN; otherwise the code will stay.

title: Manufacturer - PCM/ECM Keep-Alive Communication Error
shortDescription: PCM keep-alive memory link lost on the proprietary bus.
fullDescription:
U1750 is set when the PCM cannot exchange keep-alive messages with another powertrain module within the specified timeout. This is a manufacturer defined code (commonly Ford) and may log after battery disconnection or reflash.

If the code self-clears after a few drive cycles and no driveability symptoms exist, it may simply be a one-time bus event.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Check battery & grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 12V battery voltage >12.4V and clean all chassis/engine grounds. Low voltage is the #1 cause of spurious U-codes.

fixSteps.title: Measure CAN bus
fixSteps.instruction: With ignition off, measure CAN-H to CAN-L resistance at DLC (should be 60 ohms). Check each bus individually if MS-CAN/HS-CAN split.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: Clear it?
faq.a: Yes; if it does not return within 3 drive cycles you can ignore it.

title: Manufacturer - Audio System Bus Fault
shortDescription: Audio/infotainment bus fault on proprietary network.
fullDescription:
U1800 indicates a fault on the manufacturer-specific audio/infotainment CAN subnet. Head unit, amplifier, and satellite receiver all share this bus.

The code often points at a single failed module dragging the bus low. Disconnect modules one at a time to identify the culprit.
safetyImpact: No safety impact; convenience only (radio/navigation may not work).

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Pull audio fuses
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect amplifier, then head unit; recheck code to isolate.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: Does this affect driving?
faq.a: No, but the alert on the dash may be distracting.

title: Manufacturer - Body Control Gateway Time-Out
shortDescription: BCM gateway failed to forward frames.
fullDescription:
U1850 is set when the body control module, acting as a gateway between HS-CAN and MS-CAN, fails to forward messages within the allowed time. Common on mid-2000s Ford Focus, Fusion, and Mercury Milan.

A failing BCM, corrupted EEPROM, or bad chassis ground at the BCM are the top causes.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Clean BCM grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Locate BCM ground points and clean to bare metal.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: Can BCM be repaired?
faq.a: Sometimes; specialist shops can reball the BCM board.

title: Manufacturer - CAN Communication Bus Fault
shortDescription: Generic manufacturer CAN bus fault indicator.
fullDescription:
U1900 is a broad manufacturer-specific code indicating 'CAN communication bus fault.' It is a pointer code — the actual fault is identified by companion DTCs in other modules.

Always diagnose U1900 in conjunction with the U0xxx and U01xx codes that set alongside it.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Measure CAN bus
fixSteps.instruction: With ignition off, measure CAN-H to CAN-L resistance at DLC (should be 60 ohms). Check each bus individually if MS-CAN/HS-CAN split.

fixSteps.title: Node-by-node isolation
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug non-critical nodes one by one and watch for bus recovery.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive?
faq.a: No, tow if ABS/airbag lights are illuminated.

title: Ford - Audio Rear Control Interface Malfunction
shortDescription: Rear seat audio controller bus failure.
fullDescription:
Ford U2000 indicates the rear entertainment subsystem has stopped communicating with the audio head unit. Limited to vehicles with factory rear DVD/screen.

Frequently caused by a pinched harness under the center console or a failed DVD player.
safetyImpact: No safety impact.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect console harness
fixSteps.instruction: Pull console trim and inspect for pinches at seat track.

faq.q: Rear wireless headphones work?
faq.a: They run off the DVD player; if nothing plays it's the player.

title: Ford - Object Detection / Rear Camera Bus Fault
shortDescription: Camera/ultrasonic module lost on bus.
fullDescription:
U2030 on Ford applications is typically associated with the reverse camera or park aid module dropping off the CAN bus. SYNC screen may display 'Camera unavailable.'

Check the tailgate harness boot first — repeated flexing breaks wires here.
safetyImpact: Driver loses reverse camera and parking sensors; increased risk of low-speed collision.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Flex tailgate harness
fixSteps.instruction: With scan tool live-data on, flex the rubber boot between body and tailgate.

fixSteps.title: Repair broken wires
fixSteps.instruction: Solder and heat-shrink each broken conductor.

faq.q: Can I splice with crimps?
faq.a: Soldered joints last longer in flex zones.

title: Ford - Parking Aid Module Lost Communication
shortDescription: Park aid module not responding.
fullDescription:
Companion to U2030 — specifically flags the park-assist module. On F-150, Escape, and Explorer the module lives behind the rear bumper and is vulnerable to road salt.

Corrosion inside the connector is the #1 cause.
safetyImpact: Parking sensors disabled.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect park aid module and clean with electrical cleaner.

faq.q: Is a used module safe?
faq.a: Yes if programmed with Ford IDS.

title: Ford - Climate Control / HVAC Module Time-Out
shortDescription: HVAC module not responding on MS-CAN.
fullDescription:
U2040 Ford indicates the automatic climate control module has fallen off the MS-CAN medium-speed network. Blower may still run in manual override but ATC features fail.

Often linked to water leaks from the windshield cowl dripping onto the HVAC module.
safetyImpact: Defrost may not operate — reduced visibility in rain/snow.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect cowl drains
fixSteps.instruction: Clear leaves/debris from windshield cowl drains.

fixSteps.title: Replace HVAC module
fixSteps.instruction: Only if water damaged; reprogram with IDS.

faq.q: Will driving defrost still work?
faq.a: Manual defrost switch may still operate if blower has direct power.

title: GM - Class 2 Data Link Fault
shortDescription: GM Class 2 bus cannot communicate.
fullDescription:
U1201 is a GM-specific code. Class 2 is the single-wire 10.4 kbps pre-CAN bus used up to ~2010. A single shorted module pulls the whole bus down.

Ground-out test: disconnect suspect modules (BCM, radio, IPC) one at a time while watching bus activity on a scope.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Scope Class 2
fixSteps.instruction: Probe the single Class 2 wire at DLC pin 2 — should show square-wave activity.

fixSteps.title: Isolate modules
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect radio first, then BCM, then IPC, rechecking after each.

faq.q: Is Class 2 the same as CAN?
faq.a: No, it's single-wire and slower; pre-dates GMLAN CAN.

title: GM - Class 2 Invalid Serial Data Reception
shortDescription: Bad serial data on GM bus.
fullDescription:
U1204 indicates a module received Class 2 data that did not pass checksum/parity validation. Often caused by EMI, but can also point to a failing sending module.

Check for aftermarket remote-start installs — cheap kits are a common EMI source.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Remove aftermarket devices
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect remote start/stereo add-ons; recheck.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: Does this affect emissions?
faq.a: Only indirectly if the PCM drops data.

title: Chrysler - CAN-C Bus Off
shortDescription: Primary CAN-C high-speed bus has gone off-line.
fullDescription:
U2100 on Chrysler/Dodge/Jeep/RAM indicates the CAN-C (500 kbps high-speed) bus is in bus-off state. All powertrain, ABS, and airbag modules drop communication.

Most common cause is a water-soaked TIPM (Totally Integrated Power Module) — a known failure on 2011-2015 Grand Cherokee and Ram 1500.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: Can I bypass the TIPM?
faq.a: No — it's the central gateway. Replace with programmed unit.

title: Generic - CAN FD Bit Rate Switch Failure
shortDescription: CAN FD bit-rate switching fault detected.
fullDescription:
U3010 indicates a node on the vehicle's CAN FD (Flexible Data rate) network failed to transition between arbitration (1 Mbps) and data phase (5-8 Mbps). Common in 2020+ vehicles using CAN FD as backbone for ADAS.

Root cause is usually a non-FD-capable module accidentally wired to an FD segment, or degraded wiring where high bit rate edges are distorted.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Scope FD bus
fixSteps.instruction: Capture SOF/BRS transitions with 500MS/s scope; verify 5Mbps eye.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: What is BRS?
faq.a: Bit Rate Switch — indicates a CAN FD frame moving to high-speed data phase.

title: Generic - CAN FD CRC Error Counter Exceeded
shortDescription: Excessive CRC errors on CAN FD bus.
fullDescription:
U3020 is logged when a node counts more than the calibrated threshold of CRC-17 or CRC-21 errors on a CAN FD segment in a defined time window. It suggests wiring noise, corrupted transceivers, or EMI coupling.

Check for nearby high-power wiring (electric power steering, HV inverter) routed alongside the CAN FD pair without adequate shielding.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Measure CAN bus
fixSteps.instruction: With ignition off, measure CAN-H to CAN-L resistance at DLC (should be 60 ohms). Check each bus individually if MS-CAN/HS-CAN split.

fixSteps.title: Reroute harness
fixSteps.instruction: Restore OEM harness routing away from HV cables.

faq.q: Does CRC error mean a broken module?
faq.a: Not necessarily — wiring is a more common culprit.

title: Generic - 100BASE-T1 Link Down
shortDescription: Automotive Ethernet link lost.
fullDescription:
U3050 indicates a 100BASE-T1 single-pair automotive Ethernet link failed to establish or dropped during runtime. Used for backbone, ADAS cameras, and infotainment on 2022+ vehicles (VW MEB, GM Ultium, Ford Mach-E).

Link negotiation is very sensitive to cable length and connector plating quality. A dirty connector = no link.
safetyImpact: Advanced driver-assist features disabled; surround-view cameras inoperative.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect T1 connector
fixSteps.instruction: Clean gold-plated pins with isopropyl alcohol and lint-free swab.

fixSteps.title: Replace harness
fixSteps.instruction: If link won't train, replace the ethernet segment per OEM procedure.

faq.q: Can I use CAT6?
faq.a: No, automotive T1 uses single twisted pair; CAT6 cannot substitute.

title: Generic - Ethernet Switch Port Disabled
shortDescription: Managed switch disabled a port due to faults.
fullDescription:
U3060 means the central vehicle Ethernet switch disabled one of its T1 ports after repeated link faults or storm-control events. Affected node will drop from diagnostics.

Used on high-end EVs with Zonal architecture (BMW iX, Mercedes EQS).
safetyImpact: Affected zone (camera/radar/ADAS) disabled.

faq.a: No, port stays disabled until cleared by factory tool.

title: Generic - Gateway Routing Table Corrupt
shortDescription: Central gateway routing table failed CRC check.
fullDescription:
U3100 is set when the central gateway (CGW) finds its internal routing table corrupted at boot. The gateway bridges between classic CAN, CAN FD, and Ethernet segments; a corrupted table breaks most inter-segment traffic.

Can be caused by a failed flash programming session or NVM wear after 10+ years of use.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

title: Generic - Secure Onboard Communication (SecOC) MAC Failure
shortDescription: Message authentication code mismatch on CAN FD.
fullDescription:
U3200 indicates the receiving module rejected a CAN FD frame because the Message Authentication Code (MAC) did not match the expected value. SecOC is specified in AUTOSAR and used on ADAS-critical frames.

Most often logged after module replacement without key provisioning, or after aftermarket diagnostic tool injection.
safetyImpact: ADAS or steering/braking subsystems may be demoted to degraded mode.

faq.q: Why can't aftermarket tools fix it?
faq.a: SecOC keys are OEM-controlled cryptographic secrets.

title: Generic - Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) Sync Lost
shortDescription: gPTP time sync lost on Ethernet backbone.
fullDescription:
U3300 is set when a module loses IEEE 802.1AS (gPTP) time synchronization on an automotive Ethernet TSN backbone. Time sync is required for deterministic ADAS fusion and audio/video streams.

Check the master clock (usually central gateway or ADAS domain controller) first.
safetyImpact: ADAS sensor fusion may degrade; surround video may de-sync.

fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: OEM software

faq.q: Is this a firmware issue?
faq.a: Often — check TSBs for gPTP patches.

title: Generic - Diagnostic Firewall Rejected Session
shortDescription: Gateway rejected a non-authenticated diagnostic session.
fullDescription:
U3500 is logged by the central gateway when a diagnostic tool attempts to access a protected module without valid PKI authentication. OEMs use this to comply with UN-R155 cybersecurity regulations.

Most likely caused by an aftermarket scan tool without the OEM subscription.
safetyImpact: No driving safety impact; cybersecurity event log.

fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Use authorized tool
fixSteps.instruction: Use factory or authorized OEM-gateway-access tool (AutoAuth, FCA Secure Gateway bypass, etc.).

faq.q: Is it a real problem?
faq.a: Usually no — it's telling you access was denied, not a fault.

title: Toyota - CAN Main Bus Off
shortDescription: Toyota CAN high-speed bus is off-line.
fullDescription:
Toyota's U1001 signals the main CAN-HS bus is off-line. All powertrain, HV, and ABS modules go silent. Often a water-damaged combination meter or failing HV junction box on hybrids.

Use Techstream to isolate; bypass suspect modules through the diagnostic connector split.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

shortDescription: Toyota engine ECU sending invalid CAN data.
fullDescription:
Toyota U1100 is a pointer code set by another module (commonly the ABS actuator) when it receives invalid data from the engine ECU. After battery disconnection, a zero-point calibration of the yaw/steering sensor may be required.

Common on 2005-2012 Camry/Corolla after a battery change.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

title: Honda - Loss of Communication with Gauge Control Module
shortDescription: Honda cluster not responding on F-CAN.
fullDescription:
Honda/Acura U1164 indicates the PCM lost communication with the gauge control module (cluster). On 2006-2015 Civic/Accord/CR-V this is typically a cluster solder joint failure or a failed F-CAN transceiver chip.

Rebuilders specialize in refurbishing these clusters for a fraction of dealer price.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

title: Honda - Loss of Communication with Steering Angle Sensor
shortDescription: Steering angle sensor dropout (Honda).
fullDescription:
Honda U1178 is set by the VSA (stability) module when it cannot communicate with the steering angle sensor on the clockspring. Commonly set after airbag/clockspring replacement without recalibration.

Perform VSA sensor neutral-position memorization with HDS after repair.
safetyImpact: Stability control disabled; reduced safety at limit.

shortDescription: GMLAN high-speed bus U1000 variant.
fullDescription:
This variant of U1000 on GMLAN (500kbps HS-CAN) indicates a loss of primary bus communication. Common on 2010+ GM vehicles with BCM-centric gateway. The BCM drives many of the cluster warning lights so a failed BCM floods the DTC list.

Use a GDS2 tool to determine which module *is* responding and which isn't.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

title: EV - Lost Communication with Battery Energy Control Module (Variant)
shortDescription: BECM lost comms variant.
fullDescription:
U029F-v2 is a restated variant logged by the VCU when the Battery Energy Control Module (BECM/BMS) fails to respond within the expected watchdog window. On GM Ultium and VW MEB vehicles this will trigger a forced shutdown of the HV contactors.

Do not attempt HV service without proper PPE and de-energization procedure.
safetyImpact: HIGH VOLTAGE HAZARD: Traction battery circuits can carry 400-800V DC. Contact can cause fatal electric shock, arc flash burns, or cardiac arrest. Only work on HV systems after proper de-energization with certified EV PPE (Class 0 gloves, face shield) and insulated tools. Do not probe orange HV cables.

title: EV - HV Battery Module Communication Fault
shortDescription: Internal HV battery module not responding to BMS.
fullDescription:
U1300-EV is set by the master BMS when one of the slave cell-monitoring boards (CSC / BMB) fails to report cell voltages and temperatures. The BMS cannot balance or protect affected modules, so it forcibly opens contactors.

Typically caused by a failed daisy-chain isoSPI or broken ribbon cable inside the battery pack.
safetyImpact: HIGH VOLTAGE HAZARD: Traction battery circuits can carry 400-800V DC. Contact can cause fatal electric shock, arc flash burns, or cardiac arrest. Only work on HV systems after proper de-energization with certified EV PPE (Class 0 gloves, face shield) and insulated tools. Do not probe orange HV cables.

title: EV - Charge Port / EVSE Communication Fault
shortDescription: No CCS/CHAdeMO handshake on charge port.
fullDescription:
U1400-EV indicates the charge port controller cannot complete PLC or CAN handshake with the EVSE (charger). The vehicle rejects AC and DC charging. On CCS, ISO 15118 PLC modem or SLAC sequence timing is the usual suspect.

Often resolved by a firmware update; otherwise the charge port controller module must be replaced.
safetyImpact: HIGH VOLTAGE HAZARD at the charge port during fault conditions. Do not probe the DC+/DC- pins of a CCS port without confirmed de-energization.

title: EV - Drive Inverter Lost Communication with VCU

U1500-EV is set when the vehicle control unit (VCU) loses high-speed CAN FD communication with the traction drive inverter. The inverter will enter active short-circuit (ASC) mode to safely dissipate regenerative energy, which may feel like sudden loss of propulsion.

This is a CRITICAL fault — vehicle will coast to a stop. HV service required.
safetyImpact: HIGH VOLTAGE HAZARD: Traction battery circuits can carry 400-800V DC. Contact can cause fatal electric shock, arc flash burns, or cardiac arrest. Only work on HV systems after proper de-energization with certified EV PPE (Class 0 gloves, face shield) and insulated tools. Do not probe orange HV cables.

title: Generic - Control Module System Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Supply voltage outside operating window.
fullDescription:
U3008 indicates the module's local supply voltage went outside its operational range (typically <9V or >16V). Alternator regulator failure is the #1 cause on the high side; failing battery on the low side.

Perform alternator ripple test and battery load test.
safetyImpact: Multiple systems may behave erratically; risk of module damage at >16V.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Check battery & grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 12V battery voltage >12.4V and clean all chassis/engine grounds. Low voltage is the #1 cause of spurious U-codes.

fixSteps.title: Alternator test
fixSteps.instruction: Measure AC ripple across battery with engine running; load-test at 2000 rpm.

faq.q: Can this damage modules?
faq.a: Yes — prolonged overvoltage kills electronics.

title: Generic - CAN FD Sample Point Error
shortDescription: Sample-point configuration mismatch on FD segment.
fullDescription:
U3030 is logged when two modules on the same CAN FD segment are configured with incompatible sample-point timings (e.g., 80% vs 75%). One usually comes from a replaced module coded by an aftermarket tool.

Recoding to OEM spec resolves.
safetyImpact: Loss of communication may disable ABS, airbag, stability control, or powertrain protections. Vehicle may behave unpredictably; avoid driving until diagnosed.

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: OEM software
fixSteps.instruction: Use manufacturer-level tool (Techstream/IDS/GDS/SDD) to read sub-DTCs and perform module relearn/programming.

faq.q: What's a sample point?
faq.a: The percentage of bit time at which the bit is read.

title: Generic - Intrusion Detection System Event
shortDescription: Vehicle IDS detected anomalous CAN traffic.
fullDescription:
U3400 is logged by the intrusion detection system (IDS) when it observes CAN traffic that violates expected patterns — e.g., spoofed CAN IDs or rate anomalies. Required by UN-R155 on 2024+ vehicles.

Almost always triggered by aftermarket OBD-II dongles or third-party diagnostic tools performing active commands.
safetyImpact: No driving safety impact; security event logged to OEM cloud.
symptoms: OEM may email owner about anomaly

fixSteps.title: Connect scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all modules' DTCs and freeze frame data; note which module set the U-code and which is missing.

fixSteps.title: Remove OBD dongle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug aftermarket dongle and clear code.

faq.q: Should I be worried?
faq.a: Usually no — most triggers are benign dongles.

Check the 48V DC-DC converter; moisture ingress is a known issue.
safetyImpact: 48V-DC-DC HAZARD: 48V is below the high-voltage threshold but can still cause painful shocks. Do not probe 48V harness with bare hands.

Check the ADAS domain controller's dedicated power rail and cooling fan; thermal shutdown from a failed fan is common.

Check for water at the module before replacing.

fullDescription:

Installing a known-good module for a test drive is the fastest isolation.

title: Invalid Data Received from Restraints Control Module
shortDescription: The receiving module reports invalid or out-of-range data from the Restraints Control module on the CAN bus.
fullDescription:
Code U0453 is set when a control module on the network receives a message from the Restraints Control module whose contents fail a plausibility, checksum or range check. The data is structurally valid (the message arrives) but the values inside are unusable.

Invalid-data faults frequently point at the sender rather than the receiver: a sensor inside the Restraints Control module is failing, internal calibration is corrupt, or the module is reporting a fault flag in its broadcast frame.

Intermittent versions of this code are commonly caused by voltage drops, ground problems, or aging connectors that briefly corrupt the data payload.
safetyImpact: Features that depend on data from the Restraints Control module may behave unpredictably or default to safe-mode operation.

causes.cause: Internal failure of Restraints Control module

symptoms: Restraints Control feature inoperative or limited

fixSteps.title: Scan all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to identify which module reports Restraints Control and which is non-responsive.

fixSteps.title: Inspect CAN wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check CAN-H and CAN-L for shorts to power, ground, or each other; look for chafed harness near connectors.

fixSteps.title: Verify terminating resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance between CAN-H and CAN-L with battery off; should read about 60 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace module
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring is good, replace the suspect module and program/configure as required.

faq.q: Is U0453 the same as a 'no communication' code?
faq.a: No. No-communication codes mean the module is silent. Invalid-data codes mean the module is talking, but its message contents fail validity checks.

title: Invalid Data Received from Telematics Unit Module
shortDescription: The receiving module reports invalid or out-of-range data from the Telematics Unit module on the CAN bus.
fullDescription:
Code U0545 is set when a control module on the network receives a message from the Telematics Unit module whose contents fail a plausibility, checksum or range check. The data is structurally valid (the message arrives) but the values inside are unusable.

Invalid-data faults frequently point at the sender rather than the receiver: a sensor inside the Telematics Unit module is failing, internal calibration is corrupt, or the module is reporting a fault flag in its broadcast frame.

Intermittent versions of this code are commonly caused by voltage drops, ground problems, or aging connectors that briefly corrupt the data payload.
safetyImpact: Features that depend on data from the Telematics Unit module may behave unpredictably or default to safe-mode operation.

title: Body Control Module Lost Communication with Climate Module
shortDescription: BCM-related communication or data fault on the body bus.
fullDescription:
U2205 is set when the body control module (BCM) experiences a communication problem with one of its slave modules. Body-bus faults are usually slower and more localized than powertrain-bus faults but can disable many convenience features at once.

Diagnosis starts at the BCM connectors. Many vehicles route the body bus through the BCM, so a single bad BCM ground or backed-out pin will cascade into multiple slave-module communication codes.

Before replacing modules, always verify proper supply voltage, ground integrity, and that no aftermarket wiring (alarms, remote starts, dash cams) is interfering with the bus.
safetyImpact: Convenience and lighting features may behave erratically or be disabled. Generally not a driving safety concern, but may affect lighting at night.

fixSteps.instruction: Check CAN-H and CAN-L for shorts to power, ground, or each other; look for chafed harness near connectors.

fixSteps.title: Verify terminating resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance between CAN-H and CAN-L with battery off; should read about 60 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace module
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring is good, replace the suspect module and program/configure as required.

title: Power Window Module Implausible Position Data
shortDescription: BCM-related communication or data fault on the body bus.
fullDescription:
U2380 is set when the body control module (BCM) experiences a communication problem with one of its slave modules. Body-bus faults are usually slower and more localized than powertrain-bus faults but can disable many convenience features at once.

Diagnosis starts at the BCM connectors. Many vehicles route the body bus through the BCM, so a single bad BCM ground or backed-out pin will cascade into multiple slave-module communication codes.

Before replacing modules, always verify proper supply voltage, ground integrity, and that no aftermarket wiring (alarms, remote starts, dash cams) is interfering with the bus.

title: Vehicle Communication Bus A Performance
shortDescription: Generic CAN bus electrical fault on a primary vehicle communication bus (A bus).
fullDescription:
U0028 is a generic OBD-II code that indicates an electrical problem on one of the vehicle's primary communication buses. 'Performance' subcodes flag intermittent or out-of-spec behavior; 'Low/High/Open' subcodes flag specific electrical states.

These low-numbered U-codes are usually network-wide problems rather than single-module problems. Many modules will store related codes simultaneously.

Start with a careful electrical inspection: termination resistance, supply voltage to all modules on the affected bus, and ground integrity at the body and powertrain ground points.
safetyImpact: Multiple safety-related modules (ABS, airbags, transmission) can be affected. Drive only as far as necessary to reach a repair location.

fixSteps.title: Scan all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use scan tool to identify which module reports primary bus and which is non-responsive.

fixSteps.title: Inspect CAN wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check CAN-H and CAN-L for shorts to power, ground, or each other; look for chafed harness near connectors.

fixSteps.title: Verify terminating resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance between CAN-H and CAN-L with battery off; should read about 60 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace module
fixSteps.instruction: If wiring is good, replace the suspect module and program/configure as required.

faq.q: Why does U0028 cause so many other codes?
faq.a: When a primary bus is electrically disturbed, every module that depends on it stores its own communication-lost code. Fixing the underlying bus problem usually clears the cascade.
